issues.description: Race condition on shared lora_config.is_registered mutation in async request handler
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request mutates lora_config.is_registered = True after loading weights. The TritonLoraConfig instance is shared across all concurrent requests. Two concurrent first-time requests can both see is_registered=False, both omit weights on second send, or worse, one marks registered before TRT-LLM has actually cached it. Needs a lock or per-request copy.

issues.description: _get_lora_config return type annotated TritonLoraConfig but returns None
issues.detail: Signature declares -> TritonLoraConfig but returns None when lora_name is None or metadata.lora_configs is None. Should be Optional[TritonLoraConfig]. Also model_metadata.get(model_name) can return None and the next line dereferences .lora_configs unguarded, causing AttributeError for unknown model names.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is not stable across model repos and not globally unique
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 per call and increments across repo_paths within one call, but the same ids can collide across different base models since TRT-LLM treats task_id as a cache key. Two models each defining LoRAs with task_id 1,2 will alias entries in the TRT-LLM LoRA cache, returning the wrong weights.

issues.description: Stray debug print and traceback dumps left in production paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the per-LoRA loop, plus print(traceback.format_exc()) in the except branch and in three FastAPI routers, will spam stdout for every request and every parse. Use logging at appropriate levels; do not unconditionally dump tracebacks to stdout in production.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path reused for two different paths in same scope
issues.detail: Line ~672 binds lora_config_path = os.path.join(version_path, "multi_lora.json"), then inside the loop reassigns lora_config_path = os.path.join(lora_path, "model.lora_config.npy"). On the second repo iteration the original multi_lora.json path is lost and the existence check / open uses the stale weights path name. Rename one.

issues.description: Return type annotation now mismatches actual return
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs is annotated -> None | List[tuple[str, str]] but returns List[TritonLoraConfig] or None. Misleading to readers and breaks any static type checking. Update to Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]].

review.summary: The PR adds multi-LoRA support for TRT-LLM in the OpenAI frontend but has a serious concurrency bug: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is mutated as shared state across async requests, opening a race where two first-time requests may both skip sending weights. lora_task_id is also assigned per parse call and can collide across base models, aliasing the TRT-LLM LoRA cache. Type annotations are stale (Optional returns declared non-Optional, tuple list declared but TritonLoraConfig returned), and lora_config_path is reused as both the multi_lora.json and the .npy path within the same scope. Debug print statements and unconditional traceback dumps were added to hot paths and should be replaced with proper logging before merge.
